data.name: Skim Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Skim milk powder (SMP) prices increased at both ends of the range this reporting period. Processor prices were up from both last month and year-ago levels, with a 41 percent improvement year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes decreased 65 percent last week compared to the week prior. SMP futures strengthened across all contract periods, increasing by as much as 1.7 percent for December. SMP exports from New Zealand were stronger in August, up 47 percent YoY and up 8 percent year-to-date. There was a 68 percent increase in volumes shipped to Asia except China, and a 171 percent growth in Middle East purchases, while shipments to China fell 28 percent.

SMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 413 increased across all offered contract periods, led by January, which was up 4.8 percent. No product was offered for March or April. December and January accounted for 79 percent of total sales. Total volume sold was lower than Event 412 and slightly below year-earlier levels. Southeast Asia/Oceania was the top buyer, purchasing 47 percent of the total volume, which was down from 60 percent from the previous event but up from 28 percent a year ago. North Asia followed with 42 percent. SMP reached its highest average price since July 2022 and up 48 percent from year-ago levels.

data.name: Whole Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Whole milk powder (WMP) prices moved higher at the bottom of the range, while sliding lower at the top this reporting period. Processor prices decreased from last month and are 6 percent lower compared to year-ago levels. Futures trading volumes decreased 16 percent last week compared to the week prior. WMP futures were higher for October; steady for December; and lower for November, and January through March. The February future contract saw the largest decline, down 1.1 percent. New Zealand's WMP exports rose 22 percent in August and 12 percent year to date, driven by sharply higher shipments to China (+64 percent), other Asian markets (+28 percent), and the Middle East (+59 percent).

WMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 413 increased across all contract periods offered, led by February, which was up 1.8 percent. No product was offered for March or April. December and January accounted for 77 percent of total sales. Sales volumes were lower than both Event 412 and year-earlier levels. North Asia was the top buyer, purchasing 45 percent of the volume, up from 40 percent at the previous auction and down from 56 percent a year ago. Southeast Asia/Oceania bought 28 percent of the volume, followed by the Middle East.

data.name: Cheddar Cheese
data.narrative:
Cheddar cheese prices moved lower at the top of the range, but held steady at the bottom this reporting period. Processor prices were down from last month and are 17 percent below year-ago levels. New Zealand cheese exports were up 24 percent year-over-year and were higher to Asia.  

At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 413, cheddar prices were lower for all contract periods offered except November. The January contract, down 6.2 percent, had the largest loss. No cheddar was offered for the April contract at this event. Total volume sold was slightly higher than Event 412 and similar to a year ago. December and January accounted for 66 percent of all cheddar sales. Africa led purchasing, followed by Southeast Asia/Oceania and the Middle East.

data.name: Butter
data.narrative: Butter prices decreased at the top of the range, while holding steady at the bottom this reporting period. Processor prices also moved lower compared to last month and are down 31 percent year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes increased 69 percent last week compared to the week prior. Last week butter futures were steady for March; weaker for November, January and February; and stronger for October and December. August butter exports were down 8 percent YoY but up 13 percent year-to-date (YTD), due to weaker volumes shipped to Asia which offset purchase growth from Europe, Oceania, and the Middle East.At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 413, butter prices were mostly lower, with December up just 0.1 percent and the remaining offered contracts down by as much as 1.6 percent. No butter was offered for March or April. December and January accounted for 82 percent of total sales. Butter volume sold increased compared to Event 412 and was slightly below year-ago levels. North Asia led purchasing with 73 percent, followed by South/Central America and Europe. Global milk fat inventories remain elevated, bolstered by strong export growth from the US, Argentina, and Europe. Butter shipments are sharply higher year-to-date. Volumes increased 7.9 percent from the previous event and 10 percent for December offerings. Meanwhile, butter prices have fallen to their lowest level since September 2023.
